title: First part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and a translation vector of zero, zero, and zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the plane defined by this coordinate system. For the first face, start by drawing the first line from the origin (zero, zero) to the point (zero point zero one seven three, zero). Draw the second line from (zero point zero one seven three, zero) to (zero point zero one seven three, zero point seven five). Continue with the third line from (zero point zero one seven three, zero point seven five) to (zero, zero point seven five), and complete the loop with the fourth line from (zero, zero point seven five) back to the origin. Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of zero point seven five. Rotate the scaled two-dimensional sketch using the same Euler angles as before, and translate it using the same translation vector. Finally, extrude the scaled and transformed two-dimensional sketch along the normal by zero point zero one seven three units to create a three-dimensional solid body. The resulting dimensions of the first part are a length of zero point zero one seven three zero seven six nine two three zero seven six nine two three zero five units, a width of zero point seven four nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine nine units, and a height of zero point zero one seven three zero seven six nine two three zero seven six nine two three zero five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch for the rectangular top
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0173, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0173, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular top
r = r.extrude(0.0173)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
# The translation vector is [0, 0, 0], so no translation is needed
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a simple square prism (vertical post)
# Cross-section: 0.0173 x 0.0173 in XY plane
# Height: 0.75 along Z axis

side = 0.0173
height = 0.75

r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .rect(side, side)
    .extrude(height)
)
